images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A tabletop sea of frosted acrylic waves, rippled and softly glowing from within, fills a shallow graphite tray about a forearm long. Riding at its centre is a flat product-launch barge the size of a shoebox, its hull brushed graphite metal with a chamfered bow and neat rivet rows. On its deck sits a single product crate of ivory card, crisply folded and tied with graphite wire. Along the barge's rail hang four small ivory paper lifeboats on graphite davits, and one acid-lime lifebuoy is clipped at the stern. A folded ivory launch plan rests on the tray rim at left, weighted by a graphite paperweight. Fine scuffs mark the hull, and dust sits in the wave grooves. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama, captured mid-disaster. The same barge listing hard to the right. Its bow has dipped under the frosted acrylic waves, and the ivory product crate slides down the tilted deck, its wire snapped and one corner already in the water. Three of the four paper lifeboats have been cut loose from the budget and hang mid-fall from their davits, graphite lines coiling after them; the fourth dangles by one end. The acid-lime lifebuoy has jumped its clip and is caught in the air over the stern. Frosted spray lifts where the bow meets the waves. On the left, the launch plan has been swept off the tray rim and flutters open. Crumpled paper scraps drift on the surface, spreading outward from the hull. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. The hero object stays slightly left of centre, and the spread of the disaster runs to the right and toward the camera so its path can be traced back to the source. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: the same soft upper-left key and right-side bounce fill as a calm studio setup, unchanged, so the disorder reads as physical and real rather than theatrical. Airborne paper, grains and fragments catch the key light with crisp edge highlights. Camera: 85mm lens at f/5.6, same three-quarter tabletop angle, fast shutter freezing everything mid-air. Focus sits where the chain reaction started, and the spread softens into the depth of field. Mood: absurd but plausible, an orderly system that got out of hand, still clean and editorial. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A deep miniature sea floor of pale sediment stretches into dim, milky distance, lit from above through a ceiling of frosted acrylic waves. In the foreground lies the giant barge, broken in two across its middle, its graphite hull crusted with pale paper silt and its davits bent. The product crate has burst open on the seabed, its ivory card walls softened and collapsed. Three paper lifeboats lie scattered across the floor like pale husks. In the midground, a slim graphite salvage rig hangs from a vertical cable that rises out of frame, and its lime grab claw closes around one intact product carton, lifting it upward in a thin plume of silt toward a small graphite pontoon floating dark on the surface above. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: soft overcast late-afternoon daylight still falling from the upper left, with long soft shadows grounding the ruins and atmospheric haze fading distant forms into pale grey-green. Camera: wide 24mm view from a low vantage just above the terrain, deep focus through the midground, with a gentle tilt-shift falloff at the top and bottom edges so the vast scene still reads as a miniature diorama.
